Your recovery essentials.

All four services are available in the Recovery Room. Choose PEX open access or a private reservation.

Westwood

Infrared sauna

Gentle infrared warmth for a slower moment in your day.

Benefits & considerations

Why try it. A warming, restful experience; some small studies report improvements in pain and well-being.

What to know. Evidence is limited, and findings from traditional saunas do not automatically apply to infrared sessions.

Before you try. Check with your clinician before use if pregnant or if you have heart or blood-pressure conditions. Avoid heat when unwell or dehydrated; stop if dizzy.

Research review ↗ · Heat & pregnancy ↗

Westwood

Cold plunge

A cool-water immersion experience, on its own or alongside warmth.

Benefits & considerations

Why try it. May reduce muscle soreness after strenuous exercise compared with rest alone.

What to know. Short-term relief does not mean faster muscle growth or proven long-term health benefits.

Before you try. Cold water changes breathing, heart rate, and blood pressure rapidly. Speak with your clinician first if you have heart, circulation, or breathing conditions. Do not plunge alone or hold your breath.

Recovery evidence ↗ · Cold-water safety ↗

Westwood

Normatec compression

Rhythmic air compression around your legs while you recline.

Benefits & considerations

Why try it. May offer modest relief from post-exercise soreness and the feeling of tired legs.

What to know. Studies show small or inconsistent effects on strength and performance recovery.

Before you try. Do not use with known or suspected blood clots, acute infection, or acute heart failure. Ask the team and your clinician about wounds, fractures, or circulation concerns before use.

Recovery review ↗ · Manufacturer safety ↗

Westwood

Red light therapy

Red and near-infrared light in the Westwood Recovery Room.

Benefits & considerations

Why try it. Some targeted light-treatment trials show improvements in fine lines and skin appearance with repeated use.

What to know. Results depend on dose and device. Facial-device studies do not establish results for our panel; whole-body exercise-recovery evidence remains uncertain.

Before you try. Check first if you take light-sensitizing medication or have a light-sensitive condition. Follow the device instructions and the team’s eye-protection guidance.

Skin trial ↗ · Whole-body review ↗ · Safety guidance ↗

Benefits vary by person, equipment, and session. These notes are a starting point, not a complete contraindication list or medical advice. Ask your healthcare professional about suitability and tell our team about relevant conditions before your visit. Medical disclaimer (PDF) ↗
